articles.title: Fantasy Football: Can the surprise players of the first half of the 2026 season keep it rolling?
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Matt Harmon examines some of the top surprise players of 2026.
articles.body:
Jordan Love, Packers FPTS/G: QB4 Preseason: QB18 (+14)

Jordan Love has been one of the NFL's most prolific passers this season. Frankly, this one was easy to see coming, but the fantasy community let Love slip to the late rounds while chasing all his pass-catchers. That math didn't add up.

The Packers' run game was destined to take a step back with Josh Jacobs' turbulent offseason and the degradation of their offensive line. Green Bay is up 19 spots in total pace of play from last season and is second in pass-rate over expected. The theory of the case played out.

The offense is built around Love as a downfield passer launching the ball to two excellent and ascending wideouts in Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. I don't see any reason why this would change.

C.J. Stroud, Texans FPTS/G:QB5 Preseason: QB22 (+14)

C.J. Stroud's ascension is similar to Love's; the offense is now built around the quarterback. Houston ranks sixth in pass rate over expected in 2026 and first in adjusted yards per attempt when it gets five pass-catchers out in the route. The Texans can spread the field with a ton of eligible receivers and let their quarterback cook. He's responded with easily his best pro season.

Stroud was simply unfairly maligned for a horrific showing in the NFL playoffs last year. Yet, he was a top-10 quarterback by EPA per dropback in 2025. Now, he's surrounded by a deep and diverse set of aerial weapons for the first time in years. I think he will continue to roll.

Kirk Cousins, Vikings FPTS/G: QB8 Preseason: N/A

When he's been kept clean this year, Kirk Cousins has performed like a top-10 quarterback. The Raiders are the 11th-best unit in my offensive efficiency metrics, despite having a poor rushing attack. They are up this high because Cousins executed Klint Kubiak's well-designed pass game at a high level.

Now, he heads to Minnesota to retake his gig as the starting quarterback in a Kevin O'Connell offense he knows well. Cousins may not have to throw the ball as much with the Vikings defense in peak form. That could lead to a dip in his overall raw production, but he should still be quite efficient.

Kenneth Walker III, Chiefs FPTS/G: RB2 Preseason: RB7 (+5)

Kenneth Walker III has been a complete identity-changing force for the Kansas City Chiefs . He should have been a top-12 selection in fantasy drafts this summer but was a total steal in Round 2.

The Chiefs rank first in EPA per rush on their running back runs and are second in explosive rushing rate. That's wildly different from the team they were in previous seasons. Unless Walker gets hurt — knock on every piece of wood in your home — this train isn't stopping.

Chuba Hubbard, Panthers FPTS/G: RB6 Preseason: RB33 (+27)

Chuba Hubbard has handled a whopping 78% of the Panthers' running back touches in 2026. The only backs who have handled a higher share of the backfield work for their teams are Jahmyr Gibbs, James Cook III and the aforementioned Walker. He's been on the field for 81% of the team's snaps; no other back has cleared 80%.

Hubbard has been given Round 1 fantasy running back workhorse-level touches and the Panthers offense, even with some recent struggles, is hanging onto the 10th spot in my offensive efficiency metrics. It's simple: if you almost never leave the field and get workhorse volume in a good offense, you're a high-end RB1 in fantasy.

Bucky Irving, Buccaneers FPTS/G: RB7 Preseason: RB20 (+13)

The revival of Bucky Irving has been one of my favorite developments of the season. As a rookie, Irving was a revelation as an explosive screen-receiver and power runner. He slipped last year due to injuries but is all the way back this year.

Irving is the engine of the Tampa Bay offense. The Bucs rank dead last in EPA per dropback but 13th as a rush unit. That 19-point gap is the third-largest in favor of the run game among all NFL offenses. Over the last month, Tampa Bay has leaned into more gap-scheme runs, which is Irving's specialty, but it still leads the NFL in yards per carry on zone runs by running backs. With an elite defense and Baker Mayfield still struggling, the Bucs should run heavy ground-and-pound game scripts going forward.

Jaylen Warren, Steelers FPTS/G: RB9 Preseason: RB27 (+18)

For years, we've all wondered why the Steelers coaching staff didn't unleash a clearly electric talent in Jaylen Warren as the lead back. We finally got our wish this year, even if it took an injury to Rico Dowdle to get Mike McCarthy and Co. to tilt the scales to Warren. For three weeks when Dowdle missed time (Weeks 3 to 5), Warren handled over 90% of the backfield touches and averaged 22.3 points per game.

Since Dowdle has returned, Warren is still the lead back but has seen his workload share dip to 58%. He's still been quite good, averaging 14.9 points per game, but is settling into more high-end RB2 production. That's totally fine and still makes him one of the best picks on the board. The Steelers have an even larger gap (23 spots) than the Bucs' between their rush and pass EPA. Pittsburgh should keep leaning on both backs as the offense's leading actors.

WRs Christian Watson, Packers FPTS/G: WR5 Preseason: WR27 (+22)

Christian Watson, Packers FPTS/G: WR5 Preseason: WR27 (+22)

With Jordan Love, as discussed above, dominating as a passer this season, he's taken both of his top two receivers with him. The Packers are now one of the most concentrated passing offenses in the NFL. They rank third in target share to their top three players and first in air yard share to their top two. Losing Jayden Reed for the season has further boosted what was always going to be excellent seasons for Christian Watson and Matthew Golden.

As for Watson, it was a miracle he put up what was clearly his best season on tape in 2025, despite coming back from an ACL tear in January of that year. Yet, he's taken another step up this year, as a high-end ball-winner and full-field route runner against man coverage. No receiver over the last five seasons has improved more than Watson.

Matthew Golden, Packers FPTS/G: WR8 Preseason: WR47 (+39)

Despite Watson's excellent play, second-year receiver Matthew Golden leads the team in targets and air yards. He's been a revelation for this team after he moved from a nebulous role as a rookie to a featured X-receiver in Year 2.

Beyond the structural changes we highlighted above in the Love section, Golden has also made massive strides as an individual player. He wasn't bad on tape in 2025, but he's still destined to be the most improved wide receiver in the NFL from 2025 to 2026.

The wild part: Golden isn't done getting better. Golden has dropped an NFL-high 10 passes (second closest is six) and only won two of seven contested catches, per Fantasy Points Data. I actually think Golden has good tracking, late hands and catch technique; he's just suffered mental lapses and focus drops. The good news is that Love doesn't care and keeps firing the ball to him right after his mistakes. Last week, as Golden caught all 10 of his targets for a season-high 164 yards and a touchdown against a good secondary, is a reminder of why you keep the faith in these guys.

Tee Higgins, Bengals FPTS/G: WR4 Preseason: WR15 (+11)

Tee Higgins was such a fantastic draft pick this year. It is and was another simple case. As long as Higgins and Joe Burrow are both healthy and available to play, the gifted receiver produces like a WR1 in fantasy football despite sharing the field with Ja'Marr Chase.

This year, though, he's been even better. The Bengals flirted all offseason with changing their offense to a more under-center and run-oriented attack to stick with the current NFL meta. It didn't take long for them to ditch that idea. Through nine weeks, the Bengals rank 31st in under-center rate and lead the league in pass rate over expected. The Bengals are essentially running an air-raid offense, and it's been a joy to watch.

As for Higgins himself, he leads the league in yards gained on dig and post routes this year. Those chunky, downfield in-breakers haven't always been his specialty. He's typically operated as a sideline ball-winner. He's now blended both styles to produce like a top-five wideout.

Isaiah Likely FPTS/G: TE3 Preseason: TE13 (+10)

For the most part, tight end has met expectations and is really just a mess beyond a small handful of players. Not that there is anything unusual about that. As such, when you get a hit like Isaiah Likely has been for drafters, it moves the needle.

Likely was one of my favorite picks on the board for most of the summer, before we started to get positive Malik Nabers injury updates. I should have held strong. Just over 56% of the Giants' passing targets go to their top two options in Nabers and Likely. That is the highest rate in the NFL. Regardless of who is at quarterback, these two guys have thrived. I have to give credit to Greg Roman and Matt Nagy; they've done a fantastic job of designing route concepts to use these two in tandem.

articles.title: The Top-50 NFL Players In The First Half Of The 2026 Season, Ranked
articles.summary: Who has been the best player so far in the NFL this season? We rank our top 50 players in the league.
articles.body: Who is the best player in the NFL? For the first handful of years of the 2020s, you could've easily answered that question by saying "Patrick Mahomes." But as the Kansas City Chiefs' star quarterback is in his first year back from an ACL tear, Mahomes isn't the shoo-in answer he once was to that question. And there are plenty of quarterbacks who have staked their claim to be considered the best in the league so far in the 2026 season. And looking beyond the most important position in football, there are several other players who have dominated across the league over the first nine weeks of the year. So, along with our eye in the sky Bucky Brooks, we ranked the top 50 players so far this season. We did use positional value to help shape the list, but quarterbacks don't entirely dominate our top 50. 50. RB Christian McCaffreySan Francisco 49ers Steven Ruiz: Kyle Shanahan is trying his hardest to cut McCaffrey’s workload, but it’s difficult to resist the allure of giving him the football. When he’s out on the field, he’s been the focal point of the powerful 49ers offense. He’s still making defenders miss at a high rate, and he’s still getting open on every route he runs. Shanahan’s restraint over the first half should make McCaffrey even better over the second half of the season. Stat to know: McCaffrey has scored a touchdown in seven of his eight games this season (10 total touchdowns: nine rushing, one receiving). Following his 2,126-scrimmage-yard season in 2025, he has produced 27 total touchdowns in his last 25 regular-season games. 49. Edge Abdul CarterNew York Giants Henry McKenna: Carter just pops on film, with an explosiveness, disruptiveness and playmaking ability that the Giants must love. It has been fun to see Carter and Arvell Reese operate together as one of the most hard-to-handle young playmaking tandems in the NFL. New York has asked a lot of its defense in the early weeks of the season — what with the QB situation changing weekly. That has made Carter’s contributions all the most impressive. Stat to know: Carter has generated 30 quarterback hits and six sacks in 25 games since entering the league with the Giants, recording at least one quarterback hurry or hit in 19 of those 25 appearances. 48. S Evan WilliamsGreen Bay Packers Ruiz: Williams can line up anywhere in Green Bay’s amorphous defense, and he seems to make plays wherever the Packers deploy him. He can be the last line of defense as a deep safety; drop into the box to defend the run; cover from the slot; or rush off the edge. He’s done it all at a high level in 2026. He’s made 48 tackles, intercepted three passes, defended seven more, and even generated 14 pressures as a pass rusher. Stat to know: Williams leads all Green Bay defensive backs with 71 total tackles and three interceptions through nine games, making him the only safety in the NFC this season with at least 70 tackles and 3+ interceptions. 47. WR Amon-Ra St. BrownDetroit Lions McKenna: For all the splash plays that come from Jameson Williams and Gibbs, St. Brown is churning out catches and first downs when the team needs him most. It’s not always pretty. And it doesn’t always look impressive, given all the amazing stuff that the Lions do offensively. But St. Brown is one of the best and most reliable receivers in the NFL. Keep in mind: He had five touchdowns in the first three games. He hasn’t scored since. I think he’s overdue. Stat to know: St. Brown has caught at least six passes in seven of Detroit's eight games this season. Coming off a 117-catch campaign in 2025, he has recorded five-plus receptions in 23 of his last 25 regular-season games. 46. OT Amarius MimsCincinnati Bengals Ruiz: The Bengals have spent the last few years trying to build a formidable pass protection for Joe Burrow, and Mims is the biggest hit yet. He’s looked impossible to beat in pass protection so far this season, allowing just five pressures across 319 pass snaps. Mims is a big, strong dude with quick feet, and his technique is always improving. His ability to hold up on an island is a big reason why Cincinnati can call pass plays at a high rate without exposing Burrow to too many hits. Stat to know: Mims has yielded only five total pressures (one sack, three hits, one hurry) across 334 pass-blocking snaps at right tackle in 2026, posting a pass-blocking efficiency rate of 98.5%. 45. C Zach FrazierPittsburgh Steelers McKenna: A center? In the top 50?! In this economy!?!? Frazier is, simply, the best player on the Steelers offense. Jaylen Warren is a nice player — perfectly fine. But he’s popping off big runs in large part because of the way Frazier is helping them own the line of scrimmage. It is basically their entire offensive identity. With Aaron Rodgers (and DK Metcalf) looking old, I don’t know how the Steelers would move the ball without Frazier. Stat to know: Frazier has played 343 pass-blocking snaps at center this season without surrendering a single sack, anchoring Pittsburgh’s interior line with only seven total pressures allowed all year. 44. OT Dion DawkinsBuffalo Bills Ruiz: Dawkins is the best offensive lineman on perhaps the NFL’s best offensive line. The hulking tackle just wears down defensive linemen in the run game, and he’s a big reason why the Bills' run game has been so successful. There’s a reason head coach Joe Brady loves to call runs to the left side. Dawkins doesn’t have the lightest feet, which can get him into trouble against certain pass rushers, but he’s far from a liability in pass protection. Stat to know: Dawkins has allowed just two sacks on 265 pass-blocking snaps this season, and Buffalo's offense has surrendered zero sacks off his edge in five of his seven starts in 2026. 43. LB Carson SchwesingerCleveland Browns McKenna: The Browns don’t have many elite playmakers, which begs the question of how in the world they’re 5-4. (Credit to Todd Monken!) But Carson Schwesinger is the top dog in Cleveland. They win based on this young defensive core, from Denzel Ward to Schwesinger to Jared Verse. Those are their three playmakers at the three different levels. And DC Mike Rutenberg has each of them playing like some of the best players at their positions. Stat to know: Schwesinger has posted double-digit total tackles in five separate games this season, leading Cleveland with 89 tackles (40 solo, 49 assisted) while adding 3.0 sacks in nine games. 42. CB Derek Stingley Jr.Houston Texans Ruiz: By Stingley’s standards, 2026 has been a "down year" for the Texans cornerback. He’s still been very good, allowing only 1.1 yards per coverage snap, per Next Gen Stats. Stingley remains sticky in coverage, but a few unfortunate lapses at the catch point have dragged down his numbers. Still, Stingley is as complete a cornerback as you’ll find. He can play man, he can play zone, and few defensive backs can match his ball skills. Stat to know: Stingley has broken up at least one pass in six of Houston’s eight games this season. Since 2025, his 22 passes defensed and five interceptions rank among the top three boundary cornerbacks in the AFC. 41. Edge Dallas TurnerMinnesota Vikings McKenna: Turner’s ascent has been rapid in 2026. He already has nearly as many sacks this year (7) as he did in 17 games last year (8). And that’s because he’s earned himself a role as an every-down player. Last year, he played just 65% of snaps. This year, he’s up to 80%. That’s why all his statistics are surging, including pressures, where he is tied for fourth in the NFL (41). He’s turning into the perfect queen on Brian Flores’ chessboard. Stat to know: In his third NFL season, Turner has produced 7.0 sacks and 20 quarterback hits in his first eight games, joining Danielle Hunter as the only Vikings edge rushers in the last decade to reach 20 QB hits prior to Week 10. 40. Edge Maxx CrosbyLas Vegas Raiders Ruiz: Crosby isn’t putting up gaudy sack numbers, but he remains one of the NFL’s most complete edge defenders. He’s a disruptive force who can cave in a pocket or blow up a run play in the backfield. The sack numbers may not be there, but Crosby is due for some positive regression in that category. His 44 pressures rank third behind Rousseau and Hutchinson, per Pro Football Focus. Another underrated aspect of Crosby’s game: he rarely comes off the field. He leads all edge defenders with 505 snaps played. Hutchinson is second at 468. Stat to know: Crosby has registered 33 tackles for loss in 24 regular-season games since the start of 2025, leading all NFL defensive edge rushers in backfield stops over the last two seasons. 39. WR Christian WatsonGreen Bay Packers McKenna: It’s a joy to watch a player ascend in the manner that Watson has. Going back to 2024, he had elite speed and a set of routes that worked well. But he was far from a complete player. And then the Packers spent most of 2025 running the football and containing their passing offense. Watson missed five games, which has always been a part of the issue with him. And it felt like he was on the verge of stringing it all together, if he could stay healthy. Well, viola. Watson has the fourth-most receiving yards and he has seven touchdowns, already tied for his career-high. He can do a multitude of things for the Packers offense, but his ability to create deep separation has made him a meteoric talent in 2026. Stat to know: Watson has seven touchdown catches through nine games this season and has averaged 17.9 yards per reception on 49 catches, making him the only receiver in the NFL in 2026 with 45-plus catches, 850-plus yards, and seven-plus touchdowns. 38. G Quenton NelsonSeattle Seahawks Ruiz: You don’t need to be an offensive line expert to watch Nelson’s tape and realize you’re watching a special player. The dude is a bulldozer in human form, displacing defensive linemen with ease and clearing out holes for his running backs. It will be easier to appreciate Nelson’s talent now that he’s playing for a true contender in Seattle. The Seahawks made that move to improve their run game, but Nelson also shores up the team’s pass protection. He’s allowed just seven pressures this season. Stat to know: Across 321 pass-blocking snaps split between Indianapolis and Seattle this season, Nelson has not allowed a single sack, extending his streak to 18 consecutive regular-season starts without giving up a quarterback takedown. 37. Edge Greg RousseauBuffalo Bills McKenna: I don’t get the sense that many folks recognize the monster that Rousseau has developed into. He’s tied for second-most sacks in the NFL at eight. He’s tied for sixth in the NFL in pressures (40). We saw the Bills' defense finally dominate an opponent — albeit Carson Wentz. And I can’t help but wonder if Rousseau and his DC, Jim Leonhard, might be onto something in the second half of the season. Can they keep ascending? Stat to know: Rousseau has recorded at least one quarterback hit in all eight games this season and has already amassed 25 QB hits and 8.0 sacks, putting him on pace to break Buffalo’s single-season quarterback hits record. 36. Edge Chase YoungNew Orleans Saints Ruiz: After a slow start to his career, Young is now living up to the pre-draft hype that got him drafted second-overall in 2020. His 8.0 sacks are just behind the league lead, and his 19.7% pass-rush win rate ranks second, per Pro Football Focus. Young is an intimidating presence on the edge of the defense, whether he’s rushing the passer or defending the run. His 34-inch arms let him ward off blockers until it's time to disengage and land an explosive hit on the poor soul with the ball. Stat to know: Young has tallied eight sacks through New Orleans’s first eight games this season, recording at least a half-sack in six different contests and matching his career high for sacks in a single season. 35. QB Dak PrescottDallas Cowboys McKenna: It’s a double-edged sword with Dak, who has monster years of production (like this one), because Jerry Jones is seemingly only willing to invest in offense. So Dak lights up the scoreboard while his defense lets opponents do the same. And then — tale as old as time — the coach botches the end-of-game situations often enough for the Cowboys to live just below .500. I think Dak has the potential to be a Top 10 player, if paired with a talented head coach. But Brian Schottenheimer isn’t that guy. So here is Dak … a good player. Not a great one. Stat to know: Prescott has thrown for 250-plus yards in seven of Dallas’s nine games this season. With 16 touchdown passes in 2026, he is one of only four active quarterbacks with eight career seasons of at least 15 passing touchdowns before Week 10. 34. QB C.J. StroudHouston Texans Ruiz: Whatever questions the Texans had about their quarterback have been answered this season. Stroud has left no doubt: he is a quarterback worth paying. He’s shored up his accuracy, and his play under pressure has improved dramatically. Through the first half, he’s been the NFL’s best quarterback against the blitz. Those were the big concerns that were preventing Houston from going all-in on the 25-year-old. The longer the team waits to pay him, the higher the price will be. Stroud ranks fifth in passer rating, and he’s averaging 8.0 yards per attempt. If he maintains those numbers, he could be the league’s highest-paid quarterback in a few months. Stat to know: Stroud has thrown multiple touchdown passes with zero interceptions in five of his eight starts this season, leading the NFL in games with two-plus pass touchdowns and no turnovers. 33. OT Darnell WrightChicago Bears McKenna: Wright is allowing an absurd 3.77 seconds in time to pressure, with just three sacks allowed. His pressure totals (36) are actually on the high side, but that time to pressure is what excuses Wright (and points more to his QB for holding onto the football). But it’s not just the passing game where Wright excels. He’s a huge part of the Bears’ power run game, where D’Andre Swift is playing out of his mind. Bears coach Ben Johnson loves Wright. It’s why the tackle got a massive extension this offseason. Stat to know: Wright has surrendered just one sack and 12 total pressures across 376 pass-blocking snaps at right tackle this season, anchoring a Chicago pass-protection unit with a pressure rate allowed under 3.2%. 32. Edge Nik BonittoDenver Broncos Ruiz: Bonitto is behind the statistical pace he’s set the last few years, but he hasn’t been any easier to block. Few offensive tackles can keep up with the fifth-year pro when he fires off the ball. He’s so quick off the line, he doesn’t have to do much hand fighting to get by a blocker. His bend lets him turn the corner to get to the quarterback. The numbers may be down, but Binitto has played his best lately. He could be in for a huge second half. Don’t be surprised if he outplays this ranking down the stretch. Stat to know: Bonitto has racked up 18.5 sacks and 39 quarterback hits across 26 regular-season games dating back to Week 1 of 2025, giving him the most multi-sack games (5) on the Denver defense over that span. 31. CB Devon WitherspoonSeattle Seahawks McKenna: During the Seahawks’ Super Bowl run, Witherspoon established himself as one of the best cover corners. During the Seahawks’ Super Bowl win, he shocked everyone — especially Drake Maye — by debuting his elite blitzing abilities. Then the Seahawks paid him to keep doing it in Seattle. Which is exactly what has happened. The Seahawks' defense hasn’t been quite as elite. But Witherspoon’s quality of play hasn’t wavered. Stat to know: Witherspoon has recorded at least five tackles in eight of Seattle's nine games this season. With 56 total tackles and five tackles for loss in 2026, he is one of only two NFL cornerbacks currently leading their team's secondary in both categories. 30. DT Dexter Lawrence IICincinnati Bengals Ruiz: Lawrence has been everything the Bengals could have hoped for when they traded a first-round pick for him in the offseason. He leads the NFL in run stuffs and has been a productive pass rusher with 29 pressures. Only three interior defensive linemen have generated more. His five sacks tie him for third among that group. Lawrence has been a force multiplier for an overachieving Bengals defensive line, and he’s helped protect the linebackers, the team’s biggest weakness. Stat to know: In his first eight games with Cincinnati, Lawrence has compiled 5.0 sacks and eight tackles for loss — the fastest any defensive tackle has reached 5.0 sacks in a debut season with the Bengals since modern sack tracking began in 1982. 29. CB Trent McDuffieLos Angeles Rams McKenna: Despite all the drama surrounding the Myles Garrett trade and his knee injury, McDuffie has quietly done what he always does: play like one of the NFL’s best. He’s not a flashy ballhawk. And he’s a willing run supporter. So there’s a blue-collar way that he plays the cornerback position, which doesn’t always lend itself to praise — or highlights. But McDuffie is one of the few things that have gone right for the Rams in 2026. The acquisition has been massively impactful. Stat to know: Since joining the Rams, McDuffie has already recorded two interceptions and eight passes defensed through six games in 2026, matching his entire regular-season takeaways total from the previous two seasons combined. 28. TE Trey McBrideArizona Cardinals Ruiz: McBride might be the best pure tight end in the NFL. He doesn’t run routes quite like Bowers, but he’s a better in-line blocker. I’m sure some old-school offensive coaches would take him over our TE1. McBride also has the Gronk-like ability to run through a defender’s face. He’s also one of the best red-zone weapons in the NFL. If he played for a better team — and with a better quarterback — his numbers would look even better. McBride has already hauled in 73 catches at the midway point, but they’ve produced just 598 yards. Stat to know: McBride has caught at least seven passes in seven of Arizona’s first nine games this season. After hauling in 126 catches in 2025, his 199 receptions over a 26-game regular-season span are the most by a tight end in NFL history over that stretch. 27. QB Jared GoffDetroit Lions McKenna: Every quarterback has a weakness. (Everybody has weaknesses.) Goff’s weakness is as clear as day. He struggles against pressure — and more than most QBs. And while there was a phase of the season when he seemed to be getting better, he has actually regressed back to the mean. In his career, his EPA per dropback against pressure is -.33. This year, it’s -.31. That said, the Lions know Goff’s weakness, just like everyone else. And Detroit is doing a better job than normal to prevent pressure, which is why Goff is up here with the league’s best. The Lions are back to highlighting his strengths. Stat to know: Through his first eight games of the 2026 season, Goff has thrown 15 touchdown passes against only two interceptions, joining Peyton Manning and Aaron Rodgers as the only quarterbacks since 2000 to post multiple career eight-game spans with 15-plus passing touchdowns and two or fewer picks. 26. QB Caleb WilliamsChicago Bears Ruiz: Is there a better arm in the league right now? Williams has the finesse of a Patrick Mahomes, the raw power of Josh Allen, and the ability to throw on the move of Lamar Jackson. There are still some noticeable gaps in his game, but Williams is on track to become one of the league’s best quarterbacks. If we re-ranked the top-50 at the end of the season, Williams could crack the top-10. He just needs to shore up his accuracy and avoid the catastrophic performances we saw against Minnesota and Tampa Bay. Stat to know: Across his first two seasons, Williams reached 35 career touchdown passes in his 23rd regular-season start, making him the fastest quarterback in Bears franchise history to hit the 35-touchdown milestone. 25. WR Ceedee LambDallas Cowboys McKenna: Lamb’s reemergence has been impressive, particularly as we see George Pickens fade back into clear-cut WR2 status. I thought Pickens would eat into Lamb’s workload, if I’m being honest. I thought 1) Pickens was that good, and 2) Pickens would be that motivated with his uncertain contract status. But even with added pressure and motivation from Pickens, it has been Lamb who has reasserted himself as one of the league’s elite receivers. I love the way Lamb plays, with real dominance from every receiver position in the offense. He and Dak Prescott are back to their same old stuff. Stat to know: CeeDee Lamb has 70 catches for 904 yards and seven touchdowns, setting the Cowboys' receptions record through both Week 9 and the team’s first nine games. His receiving yardage ranks second in franchise history through Week 9 and third through Dallas’ first nine games. 24. WR Tee HigginsCincinnati Bengals Ruiz: Higgins may be in Chase’s shadow, but he’s still standing out. Cincinnati’s WR1b. does everything you’d expect out of a premier receiver. He gets open deep, dominates the catch point, and separates against man coverage. He’s also got the strongest hands you’ll find in the league. Higgins is putting up numbers (67 catches, 758 yards, six touchdowns), but he’d be even more productive if he didn’t have to share targets with another superstar pass catcher. Stat to know: Higgins has three games with 140 receiving yards or more, which is tied for the most in the NFL this season. He also has a catch of 20 yards or more in six of his eight games. 23. QB Patrick MahomesKansas City Chiefs McKenna: It will be interesting to see how and if Josh Downs can change the Chiefs' offense. For years, the Chiefs offense has constricted tighter and tighter to the line of scrimmage, with the defense controlling KC’s offense, in large part because of a lack of impact pass-catchers. Travis Kelce’s game is deteriorating. Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy haven’t become the threats that the Chiefs thought they’d be. I’m not totally bought in on the idea that Downs will suddenly realize his potential — particularly when plopped into this offense at midseason. But he can only help. And if he brings something explosive, then we could see Mahomes rise up this list. Because he’s playing well — but mostly stepping aside to let Walker carry the offense. Stat to know: Earlier this season, Patrick Mahomes earned his 100th career win in his 131st start, tying Tom Brady as the fastest quarterback to reach 100 wins in NFL history. 22. CB Denzel WardCleveland Browns Ruiz: By the numbers, Ward has been the best cornerback in the NFL this season, allowing only 129 yards on 335 coverage snaps, per Pro Football Focus. That leads all cornerbacks with at least 250 coverage snaps. Ward has been targeted only 36 times this season, and there’s a reason why quarterbacks avoid him. He’s sticky in coverage and will fight receivers for the ball, as evidenced by his three interceptions and three pass breakups. Ward has given up two touchdowns, which pushed him down this list a few spots. Stat to know: Ward has allowed a 47.4% completion rate and just 3.8 yards per target on 38 targets in primary coverage, with no touchdowns allowed, three interceptions and nine passes defensed. 21. S Kyle HamiltonBaltimore Ravens McKenna: When a quarterback lines up before the snap, they must account for where Hamilton is on the field. It’s sort of like what Ed Reed was for the Ravens. Different players. But a similar impact. And so a QB must know where Hamilton is at all times. That’s largely because he can be anywhere and do anything for this defense. And if, at any point, the offense loses track of him, it’ll be because he’s about to make a big play. Stat to know: Hamilton leads all NFL safeties with nine tackles for loss, accounting for 15% of his 60 total tackles. He also has five passes defensed and one interception. 20. WR Puka NacuaLos Angeles Rams Ruiz: Where would the Rams' passing game be without Nacua? Unfortunately, with him set to miss time, we’re about to find out. But before he got injured, Nacua was doing it all for the Rams. He can move the chains as a reliable possession receiver. He can win on vertical routes on the perimeter. And there isn’t a tougher receiver to bring down after the catch. L.A.’s dependence on Nacua drags down his efficiency, but he was still putting up impressive volume stats before the injury, averaging over 100 receiving yards per game. Stat to know: Nacua’s 70 receptions this season are the most through a player’s first seven games of a season in NFL history, breaking Adam Thielen’s record of 67 set in 2018. 19. QB Brock PurdySan Francisco 49ers McKenna: I’m going to get killed for saying this, but Purdy is starting to remind me of a mini Josh Allen. Even I know that it sounds ridiculous, part of what makes Allen so special is his sheer size. But as you can see in these rankings, a diminutive Allen (like Purdy) can be pretty darn special. He has been excellent in structure, particularly when he had two healthy receivers in Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel. With the entire WR corps getting injured, Purdy has gotten creative out of structure, using his athleticism and arm talent to generate big plays. He has taken a sizable leap in his development over the last 12 months. Stat to know: Purdy’s 104.8 career passer rating is the highest in NFL history among players with at least 1,500 pass attempts. 18. CB Christian GonzalezNew England Patriots Ruiz: If we put together this list before the Week 9 game against the Packers, Gonzalez would have been even higher. He was torched for 187 yards in the game, but had given up just 196 yards in the previous six games, according to Next Gen Stats. Don’t let one bad game fool you: Gonzalez is a lockdown corner who can travel with top wideouts thanks to his length, athleticism, and agility. There isn’t a better man coverage cornerback in the league. Stat to know: Gonzalez has not allowed a touchdown on 45 targets as New England’s top boundary cornerback. 17. WR Ja'Marr ChaseCincinnati Bengals McKenna: There’s still nothing he can’t do. Sure, his production is slightly down. But that’s not because Chase is doing anything wrong, per se. It’s just that Tee Higgins has gotten that much better, which means that he’s an absolute vacuum for targets in the Bengals offense. As has been the story for these two receivers, they have to take turns having huge games. And Higgins is enjoying more than he used to. But if you sleep on Chase — even slightly — he’ll do what he did to the Falcons last week: 10 catches, 155 yards and a touchdown. Stat to know: Joe Burrow and Chase have connected for 19 touchdowns of 40-plus yards, tying Joe Montana and Jerry Rice for the third-most by a QB-WR duo since 1980. Their 58 touchdown connections, including playoffs, moved them past Daunte Culpepper and Randy Moss for the second-most by a QB-receiver duo before both players turned 30. 16. QB Jordan LoveGreen Bay Packers Ruiz: Green Bay can’t run the ball, and its pass protection unit is among the worst in the league. That kind of offensive environment would break 99.9% of quarterbacks, but Love is thriving. He’s unshakeable in a tight pocket, and his trademark fadeaway throws help him mitigate the constant waves of pressure he faces. Love isn’t just a great thrower. He’s a sharp processor before and after the snap, which also helps him beat the rush. Stat to know: Love leads the NFL in passing yards and has 232 more than the next quarterback this season. His 2,618 passing yards is the third most through Week 9 in Green Bay franchise history (since at least 1948). 15. Edge T.J. WattPittsburgh Steelers McKenna: No one in the NFL has a faster get-off than Watt at .72 seconds, per Next Gen Stats. That’s how he’s gotten home for 7.5 sacks, the second most in the NFL. He also scored his first pick-six this year — to go with three pass breakups. Watt is the star on a Steelers defense that has been the most reliable force to get Pittsburgh to 6-2. He’s the catalyst — more than Aaron Rodgers or Jaylen Warren. Stat: Earlier this season, Watt recorded his 10th career interception, joining Julius Peppers as the only players in NFL history to record at least 100-plus career sacks and 10-plus career interceptions. 14. Edge Aidan HutchinsonDetroit Lions Ruiz: Hutchinson is Detroit’s lone source of pressure, which makes it easier for opponents to throw extra blockers at him. That hasn’t stopped the 2022 first-round pick from producing, though. His 51 pressures rank second in the NFL, per Pro Football Focus, and he’s on pace for another double-digit sack season. Hutchinson is an athletic freak with a motor that can’t be turned off. That combination makes him a true playmaker on the defensive line. Stat to know: Hutchinson is tied with Greg Rousseau for the NFL lead with 57 quarterback pressures on 341 pass-rush snaps. He also has 18 quarterback hits, sixth in the NFL, and five sacks. 13. QB Joe BurrowCincinnati Bengals McKenna: This is the type of season we’ve been hoping we’d see from Burrow and the Bengals. They didn’t fall into early holes in wins and losses. Their defense isn’t an absolute atrocity. Their offensive line can protect Burrow. The only shortcoming is the run game, which can’t seem to operate. But Burrow and his receivers have overcome that in spades, with one of the most passing offenses in the NFL. I know there’s a lot of hype around the Green Bay receivers, but I’d take the Bengals every time. And I’m sure Burrow would, too. Stat to know: Burrow has accounted for at least four touchdowns in four straight games, tying Dan Marino (1984), Drew Brees (2018) and Tom Brady (2020) for the second-longest streak since 1970. Only Peyton Manning’s five-game streak in 2004 was longer in NFL history. 12. QB Trevor LawrenceJacksonville Jaguars Ruiz: Saying a guy plays smaller than his size is not typically a compliment, but it is for Lawrence. No 6-foot-6 quarterback should be as agile as the Jaguars quarterback is. That quickness helps him navigate the pocket and remain a threat as a passer outside of it. As Lawrence gains experience, the inexplicable decisions are decreasing. He’s also shored up his accuracy. The 27-year-old is averaging 8.6 yards per attempt, which leads all quarterbacks with at least six starts. Stat to know: Lawrence ranks second in the NFL with a 111.7 passer rating, behind Joe Burrow (114.8), and leads the league with an 8.0% touchdown rate (18 touchdowns on 224 attempts). 11. OT Trent WilliamsSan Francisco 49ers McKenna: For all the jokes about the substation, it’s crazy to think that the 49ers have Warner, 10, and Williams, 38, on this list. It’s not just their longevity. It’s that they’re somehow still getting better. Brock Purdy didn’t get sacked until Week 5. Stat to know: Williams has allowed just nine pressures (one sack, two hits and six hurries) on 267 pass-blocking snaps so far this season. His 3.37% pressure rate allowed ranks third among left tackles and eighth among all NFL offensive tackles. 10. LB Fred WarnerSan Francisco 49ers Ruiz: While you can debate the top player at every other position, there’s no question who the top linebacker is. It’s Warner, and he’s held that title for the last few years. If anything, the gap is widening, as the 29-year-old just keeps getting better. He’s the best coverage linebacker in the sport. It’s like the guy has an extra set of eyes on the back of his head when he’s playing zone coverage. And now his run defense is starting to catch up. Stat to know: Warner is the only player in NFL history to record 75-plus tackles and 5-plus forced fumbles through Week 9 of a season. 9. RB Bijan RobinsonAtlanta Falcons McKenna: Robinson is still among the NFL’s elite, but I’ll admit that I’m surprised to have him at RB3 at this point in the season. And it’s not a matter of the shine coming off one of the best players in the league. He just hasn’t quite done what Gibbs or Walker have done. Because the Falcons are so often engaged in shootouts and/or are playing from behind, he’s not getting the same number of carries. He’s also seeing a humble share of the targets. He's been amazing! But he’s also trailing Gibbs and Walker in basically every statistical category. Stat to know: Robinson leads the NFL with 880 rushing yards and 665 yards after contact through Week 9. His yards after contact alone exceed the total rushing yards of all but six other NFL running backs. 8. TE Brock BowersLas Vegas Raiders Ruiz: Bowers may be listed as a tight end, but the Raiders use him as a do-it-all receiving threat. Linebackers and safeties stand no chance of covering him, and cornerbacks don’t fare much better when Bowers splits out wide. He has had some issues staying healthy early in his career, but even with two games missed, Bowers leads all tight ends in receiving yards and is tied for the league lead in touchdowns. Stat to know: Sewell has allowed just nine pressures (one sack, three hits and five hurries) on 309 pass-blocking snaps. His 2.91% pressure rate allowed ranks second among left tackles and fourth among all NFL offensive tackles. 7. RB Kenneth Walker IIIKansas City Chiefs McKenna: He has gone over 100 yards in five of his eight games as a Chief. He has also scored two or more touchdowns in five of his eight games. And it’s not like he’s racking up production based solely on his offensive line. He leads the NFL in rush yards over expected (254), per Next Gen Stats. And he’s just behind Gibbs in missed tackles forced (60). More than all that, he has been one of the most enjoyable players to watch, with the ability to pop at any moment — and against any defensive unit or alignment. Stat to know: Kenneth Walker III became the second player since 1970 to score multiple touchdowns in four of his first five games of a season, joining Calvin Johnson (2011). Walker also has five games with multiple touchdowns through the first eight games of 2026, tied with Terrell Davis (1998), Emmitt Smith (1995), Eric Dickerson (1983) and Marcus Allen (1982) for the most since the 1970 merger, trailing only Jim Brown’s six in 1958 all-time. 6. OT Penei SewellDetroit Lions Ruiz: Sewell has made the difficult transition from the right side to the left without a hitch. He’s a monster in the run game and can be used in a variety of ways. He can move defensive linemen on downhill runs or pull outside and block on the move. And while run blocking is his superpower, Sewell’s pass protection is nearly as impressive. He’s allowed just eight pressures and one sack all season. Stat to know: Sewell has allowed just nine pressures (one sack, three hits and five hurries) on 309 pass-blocking snaps. His 2.91% pressure rate allowed ranks second among left tackles and fourth among all NFL offensive tackles. 5. DT Jeffery SimmonsChicago Bears McKenna: Just after the trade, I wrote about how, in Chicago, Simmons would finally get the love he deserves as one of the best — if not the best — defensive tackles in the NFL. And that the seemingly high price would make sense when you saw Simmons on a legit defense and a winning team. Tennessee is the worst place for an elite player, because no one seems to notice them. This is the year of Simmons. He and the Bears are going to make a deep playoff run. Stat to know: The Bears are 2-0 since adding Jeffery Simmons, allowing an NFL-best 13.0% third-down conversion rate and 5.03 yards per play, down from 26.1% and 6.25 before the trade. 4. RB Jahmyr GibbsDetroit Lions Ruiz: Jared Goff will get most of the credit for Detroit’s offensive success, but there’s no doubt who serves as the engine of the unit. Everything is built around Gibbs’ ability to generate explosive plays. He leads the NFL in runs of 10 or more yards and has forced more missed tackles than anyone in the league, per Next Gen Stats. Gibbs is difficult to tackle and impossible to catch once he’s out in the open field. Stat to know: Jahmyr Gibbs’ 60 career touchdowns are tied with LaDainian Tomlinson for the second-most by any player in his first four NFL seasons, trailing only Terrell Davis (61). Gibbs needs two more to set the record. 3. Edge Will Anderson Jr.Houston Texans McKenna: He’s first in the NFL in sacks (9.5) and second in pressures (44). And in turn, he’s doing everything he can to drag a mediocre Texans defense back into relevance. The defense might be the biggest reason they’re struggling — and in (high) danger of missing the playoffs. But Anderson and C.J. Stroud are the biggest reasons why they can still make a postseason push, despite the statistical improbability. Stat to know: Will Anderson Jr. leads the NFL with 9.5 sacks, ranks second in tackles for loss (12), and ranks fourth in total pressures (47). His 9.5 sacks are the second-most through Week 9 in Texans franchise history, trailing only J.J. Watt's 10.5 in 2012. 2. WR Jaxon Smith-NjigbaSeattle Seahawks Ruiz: The Seahawks superstar is on track to win the receiving triple crown, leading the league in receptions (71), yards (1,036), and touchdowns (9). And there’s no reason to expect any slippage in the second half. Defenses have no answers for a receiver who gets open at all three levels, wins contested catches, and creates after the catch. There’s no such thing as a perfect player, but JSN gets close. Stat to know: Jaxon Smith-Njigba became the third wide receiver in the Super Bowl era to record at least 800 scrimmage yards and eight touchdowns through his first seven games of a season, joining Cooper Kupp (2021) and Jerry Rice (1986). He has topped 100 receiving yards in seven of nine games this season. 1. QB Josh AllenBuffalo Bills McKenna: There are times when it looks like he’s playing 1 vs. 11 out there — and winning. But this year, he’s also getting his whole team behind him for 11 vs. 11. And that has been when the Bills are unstoppable — when their QB1 leverages the whole offensive unit. Just because he can play hero ball doesn’t mean he should play hero ball. I think he’s getting that, and it’s making him — and the Bills — better. Stat to know: Allen is the first player in NFL history with at least nine passing touchdowns and nine rushing touchdowns through his team’s first eight games of a season. articles.title: Shedeur Sanders' Trade Market Revealed by Insider in New NFL Rumors After 2026 Deadline
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders reportedly wasn't one of the signal callers targeted ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders reportedly wasn't one of the signal callers targeted ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler said in a Thursday appearance on ESPN Cleveland he didn't think the Browns had received any calls asking after Sanders.

"My understanding is no. Maybe they got a late call, but last I checked as I was working the trade deadline on Tuesday, I was told there was nothing there," Fowler said.

The Minnesota Vikings and Baltimore Ravens completed quarterback trades ahead of the deadline by respectively acquiring Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders and Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals.

The Vikings had lost Kyler Murray to injury, while the Ravens were missing both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley at the time of the trades.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported the Vikings also made inquiries regarding the Los Angeles Chargers' Justin Herbert, Indianapolis Colts' Daniel Jones and New York Jets' Geno Smith before trading for Cousins.

Sanders made his first start of the season Sunday after starter Deshaun Watson was placed in concussion protocol following a helmet-to-helmet hit the weekend prior.

He went 19-for-31 with 297 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions while also adding 28 yards on 10 carries. The Saints ultimately won in overtime by forcing Sanders to throw an incompletion on a potential game-winning two-point conversion.

Watson, who has cleared concussion protocol, is set to start again Sunday against the visiting Houston Texans. Monken said Wednesday he expected Watson to remain starter going forward but that he considers the decision "week to week."

While Watson's return could theoretically had made Sanders expendable down the stretch of this season for the Browns, the move could have left Cleveland with Dillon Gabriel and Taylen Green as the only quarterbacks on the roster enxt season.

Watson is playing this season on the last year of his expiring contract with the Browns, while Sanders has two more seasons remaining on his rookie deal.

Cleveland.com's Mary Kay Cabot said on ESPN Cleveland ahead of the deadline she felt the Browns liked having Sanders, Gabriel and Green on their rookie deals.

"When they look ahead to next year, I think they see a very financially reasonable quarterback room, and I think they like that," Cabot said. "They've got young guys that they can develop. They've got at least one guy that they think has a chance to be their quarterback of the future in Shedeur."

Now that Sanders is officially spending the rest of the season in Cleveland, Monken could decide to give him more looks down the stretch as the Browns make a push for the playoffs while considering who will be starting for the team next season.

articles.title: New Jets Rumors Leak on Breece Hall, Geno Smith, Will McDonald, More After Trade Deadline
articles.summary: Amid another bleak season, the New York Jets were expected to move some of their valuable players ahead of the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday. Instead, they remained relatively quiet.
articles.body:
Amid another bleak season, the New York Jets were expected to move some of their valuable players ahead of the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday. Instead, they remained relatively quiet.

Jets general manager Darren Mougey was only interested in trading players on expiring contracts and wanted to keep the team's roster largely intact for the 2027 season, ESPN's Rich Cimini reported.

Jets running back Breece Hall heard his name floated in trade rumors, but the fifth-year running back just signed a three-year, $43.5 million contract extension in May. Running back Braelon Allen has emerged as a threat to take the starting role, but the Jets have been able to justify keeping both players on their roster since Allen is still on his rookie deal.

Although quarterback Geno Smith is on an expiring contract, New York never entertained the idea of the veteran, according to Cimini. Smith has provided the Jets with a decent option to evaluate rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. and tight end Kenyon Sadiq.

Jets defensive end Will McDonald IV requested a trade before the deadline, but that request was ultimately not granted. New York reportedly received a "significant" offer from the Jacksonville Jaguars, and an AFC personnel director told ESPN that McDonald could have netted the Jets a second-round pick. The fourth-year pass rusher has only started two games this season, but he is expected to see the field more often after Glenn said he earned more playing time .

The Jets received inquiries for wide receiver Garrett Wilson from the Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers, but a trade was likely never realistic. Wilson didn't want to leave and the Jets view the fifth-year wideout as a "foundational piece," according to Cimini.

Cimini believes the lack of activity signals that the Jets' front office is content with their foundation and draft capital, and they want to give head coach Aaron Glenn an opportunity to develop the current roster.

The Jets have won just two games this season and appear to be on pace for double-digit losses for the seventh consecutive season. Despite the subpar performance, Glenn believes the team is "right on the cusp of trying to breaking through."

New York holds three first-round picks in the 2027 NFL Draft. They acquired two of those selections ahead of last year's trade deadline with blockbuster deals that sent cornerback Sauce Gardner to the Indianapolis Colts and defensive tackle Quinnen Williams to the Dallas Cowboys.

This season will mark New York's 16th consecutive season without a postseason appearance, the longest active playoff drought in the league.

articles.title: Harry Kane An NFL Kicker? Patriots Star Drake Maye Supports It
articles.summary: New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye fully endorses Harry Kane’s dream of one day becoming an NFL kicker.
articles.body: New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye fully endorses Harry Kane's dream of one day becoming an NFL kicker. Maye spoke Thursday after practice at the campus of Bayern Munich — Kane's soccer team — ahead of Sunday's game against the Detroit Lions. "It would be cool to see him try," Maye said. "He’s dealt with pressure, that's one of the biggest things about kicking in the National Football League is the pressure of it. He does that for a living. So, I don’t think he’d have any problem." Kane, a longtime Patriots fan, recently became the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Ballon d’Or, soccer’s award for the best player in the world. The 33-year-old England captain this month signed a contract extension to stay at Bayern until 2029, so it’s unclear when he’d be ready to give NFL kicking a shot. Kane has mused over the years about trying it. He has even floated the idea of combining his NFL dream with joining a Major League Soccer team. "I think I’ve seen him maybe kick a few, and he looked pretty good," Maye said. "No doubt, he does that for a living, so I’m sure he’d be just fine." Jacksonville Jaguars kicker Cam Little weighed in on Kane a few days after booting a game-winning 57-yard field goal to beat the Philadelphia Eagles 19-17 in London a month ago. Little said Kane's biggest adjustment would be shifting from star striker to bit player. As a kicker, he said, "You’re out there just to back everyone up basically." Bayern is still celebrating its first Ballon d’Or winner in 45 years. It’s also the first for any player at a German club since 1996. Patriots tight end Hunter Henry said he doesn't know much about soccer but was well aware of the Bayern star: "He’s a dawg — lot of respect for Harry Kane." Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Kirk Cousins' Vikings Jersey Number Revealed in Photo After Raiders Trade
articles.summary: What's old is new for the Minnesota Vikings.
articles.body:
What's old is new for the Minnesota Vikings.

The team revealed Thursday that quarterback Kirk Cousins will wear No. 8 after arriving from the Las Vegas Raiders via trade. He wore No. 8 during his previous tenure with the Vikings, although it belonged to safety Jakobe Thomas this season.

Minnesota announced Thomas will wear No. 6.

Cousins seemed to hint this could happen Tuesday during his introductory press conference.

"I'm confident that Jakobe and I can have a healthy, mature conversation and figure this out," he told reporters .

The Michigan State product wearing No. 8 will be a familiar sight for Vikings fans, as that is the number he wore with the team from 2018 through 2023. That was one of the best stretches of his career, as he made the Pro Bowl three times and threw for more than 4,000 yards four times with the NFC North club.

Perhaps it shouldn't come as a surprise, then, that the Vikings turned to him after Carson Wentz played so poorly during Monday's loss to the Buffalo Bills. He managed to throw for just 81 yards, zero touchdowns and two interceptions while playing in place of the injured Kyler Murray.

Murray wasn't great this season either prior to his hamstring injury and has five touchdown passes to three interceptions in six games.

Despite the quarterback issues, the Vikings are still 6-2 and on the list of realistic Super Bowl contenders. That is in large part because of their dominant defense, as they likely just need even average play under center to remain a contender.

Cousins can provide just that and is fifth in the league in passing yards this season with 2,340 and second in passing touchdowns with 20.

He will look to keep that rolling in the same number he previously wore with the Vikings.

articles.title: Trevor Lawrence Reacts to Jaguars' Trade Deadline Moves, Hypes the Addition of 'Winners'
articles.summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars are pushing all of their proverbial chips to the middle of the table. After the Jaguars' brass made three significant acquisitions ahead of the NFL's trade deadline, quarterback Trevor Lawrence told reporters on Wednesday that the moves signified the organization's confidence in the team.
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars are pushing all of their proverbial chips to the middle of the table. After the Jaguars' brass made three significant acquisitions ahead of the NFL's trade deadline, quarterback Trevor Lawrence told reporters on Wednesday that the moves signified the organization's confidence in the team.

"I think we're a really good team and now we got even better with these guys," Lawrence said, per the team's website . "That's all it is, making our team even better. We know we're going to have a shot. We just have to keep playing well and we have to keep winning."

Jacksonville prioritized fortifying their defense, and they accomplished that goal by acquiring defensive tackle Jordan Davis from the Philadelphia Eagles, Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates III from the Atlanta Falcons and defensive tackle Davon Godchaux from the New Orleans Saints.

Jacksonville traded away five picks in total, including a first-round selection in the 2027 NFL Draft and two future second-round selections.

"I think to get winners, to get guys that have been there before, that experience is important," Lawrence said, via NBC Sports' Myles Simmons . "I think that is, why would you not want that if you can? Obviously, you got to look at the players you're getting, and you want great players, but if they've also won Super Bowls and been to Super Bowls, I think that's icing on the cake or whatever. That's a plus. So, we have some guys obviously in that group that have done that. Just excited to get that experience. I think they've played meaningful football. They know what it looks like and going to add that value to our team."

The Jaguars have a clear path to win the AFC South division and currently sit as the third seed in the AFC with a 6-2 record. Jacksonville finished the first half of the 2026 season with the fourth-best scoring offense and the second-best scoring defense, but Jacksonville's defense has allowed significant passing yards. Bates' experience could help the secondary bring that figure down while Davis and Godchaux help collapse the pocket and stifle the run.

The Jaguars will face the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on Sunday.

articles.title: Jordan Davis Reveals Emotional Reaction to Jaguars Trade from Eagles in New Video
articles.summary: Jacksonville Jaguars defensive tackle Jordan Davis revealed his reaction to reporters after hearing the Philadelphia Eagles traded him.
articles.body:
Jacksonville Jaguars defensive tackle Jordan Davis revealed his reaction to reporters after hearing the Philadelphia Eagles traded him.

The Jags acquired Davis for a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round selection.

Davis played five seasons for the Eagles, who selected him with the No. 13 overall pick in the 2022 NFL draft. He helped the team win a pair of NFC titles (2022, 2024) and Super Bowl LIX (2024).

Davis became a full-time starter on the defensive line in 2023. He's played and started in all 66 of the Eagles' games (including playoffs) since Week 1 of that campaign. He enjoyed his best season in 2025, amassing 72 tackles (34 solo), six quarterback hits and four-and-a-half sacks. Davis was a crucial member of an Eagles team that allowed the fifth-fewest points per game in the league.

His most iconic Eagles play occurred in Week 3 of the 2025 season, when he blocked the Los Angeles Rams' game-winning 44-year field goal attempt with two seconds remaining and returned the loose ball for a touchdown to cap a 33-26 win.

Last March, Davis signed a three-year, $78 million extension with the Eagles, keeping him under contract with the team through 2029 . However, he only played nine games with Philadelphia on that new deal, and now he's a member of a 6-2 Jacksonville team shooting for a Super Bowl after adding Davis, safety Jessie Bates and defensive tackle Davon Godchaux via trades this year.

articles.title: Jim Harbaugh Calls Out Broncos After Failed Daiyan Henley Trade, Wants NFL to Fix 'Loophole'
articles.summary: Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh wasn't pleased with the way that the Denver Broncos handled the trade between the two teams involving linebacker Daiyan Henley that ultimately fell through.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh wasn't pleased with the way that the Denver Broncos handled the trade between the two teams involving linebacker Daiyan Henley that ultimately fell through.

"The Broncos based a pass/fail on a medical grade based on whether we would take less compensation and we wouldn't, and we didn't," Harbaugh told reporters Thursday. "In my opinion, it's one of those loopholes that the league should really look into because it sets a bad precedent and continues to set a bad precedent."

"It's a loophole and teams should not have the ability to do that," he added. "It's a medical grade, it's a pass/fail for a medical grade. They told us they weren't gonna pass him if it was a fourth and a fifth, which was agreed upon, and they would not pass him for that. They would pass him for a fourth and fill in the blank. I don't know what to call that, but that's what it is."

The Broncos initially agreed to acquire Henley from the Chargers in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round pick and 2028 fifth-round pick before Tuesday's deadline, but Denver eventually canceled the swap.

"The proposed trade involving Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley will not be finalized," the Broncos said in a statement released Thursday. "We have great respect for Daiyan as a player and person, and we wish him all the best moving forward."

The failed trade came as a surprise to many, including Henley.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , Denver "had concerns" about Henley following his physical. The Broncos still discussed "revised trade alternatives throughout the day" with the Chargers, although an updated agreement wasn't reached.

Denver's new trade terms presented Los Angeles with the option of either a fourth-round pick and a seventh-rounder for Henley or a fourth-rounder and another pick flip, per Schefter .

The deal between the Broncos and Chargers wasn't the only swap that couldn't be finalized, as a trade between the Cincinnati Bengals and Philadelphia Eagles involving edge-rusher Arnold Ebiketie was also called off .

As for Henley, he's appeared in each of Los Angeles' first eight games this season. He's recorded 51 tackles, three quarterback hits, two passes defended and two tackles for loss.

articles.title: 49ers' John Lynch Reveals Initial WR Trade Target Before Pivoting to Keenan Allen at NFL Deadline
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers general manager John Lynch explained that the team initially showed interest in wide receiver Josh Downs on the trade market before ultimately acquiring veteran Keenan Allen ahead of Tuesday's deadline.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers general manager John Lynch explained that the team initially showed interest in wide receiver Josh Downs on the trade market before ultimately acquiring veteran Keenan Allen ahead of Tuesday's deadline.

"We kind of focused on Josh Downs as an option that we'd have some interest," Lynch said Thursday during a radio appearance on KNBR, via David Bonilla of 49ers Web Zone. "And Kyle and I are kind of watching Josh, and in the process, Kyle's like, 'Man, what about Keenan?' And I was like, 'You know, we hadn't given much thought to that, but let me ask about that.'

"And so, there started a conversation about two and a half weeks ago, really, when the DeForest talks [happened]. 'Would he?' And it's always fluid, and at a certain time, they didn't want to give up Keenan. It kind of wasn't going to be on the table, but we kept communicating, and ultimately we got him."

The 49ers acquired Allen from the Indianapolis Colts in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round draft pick on Tuesday.

Downs, who was also a member of the Colts prior to the deadline, was eventually sent to the Kansas City Chiefs. Indianapolis received a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2027 fifth-rounder in return.

San Francisco was able to acquire Allen at a relatively cheaper price, as the six-time Pro Bowler is nine years older than Downs.

Allen was still productive to open his 2026 campaign with Indianapolis, hauling in 40 receptions for 351 yards and one touchdown in eight games.

He'll join a 49ers receiving corps that has dealt with injuries to several contributors this year including Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, Christian Kirk, De'Zhaun Stribling and Ricky Pearsall.

As for Downs, he caught 33 passes for 354 yards and one score prior to the change of scenery.

articles.title: Human vs. ChatGPT NFL Week 10 betting picks: Ice-cold human seeks a rebound as AI gains ground
articles.summary: Week 10 NFL picks feature Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals, Kansas City Chiefs at Atlanta Falcons, and a bold over on Dolphins-Colts.
articles.body: I am officially ice cold. I followed up the disaster that was Week 8 (which I’m still not talking about) with a losing slate in Week 9. articles.title: CeeDee Lamb Describes Cowboys' Season in 1 Word, Says Beating 49ers Would 'Prove Us Right'
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb called his team's 2026 season "bittersweet" so far in a conversation with reporters on Thursday.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb called his team's 2026 season "bittersweet" so far in a conversation with reporters on Thursday.

However, the 4-5 Cowboys still have the opportunity to change the narrative surrounding this season, and a tough test awaits on Sunday when the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers roll into town.

When asked about the significance of Sunday's game, Lamb said the following, per Jon Machota of The Athletic.

"It would just prove us right. Just of how we think of ourselves throughout this building. A lot of people would be shocked, obviously, because of the record, and things that have happened leading up to this game. "But for us, we know we haven't played our best game, and we just got to go out there and do that. I feel like we play complementary football — defense gets stops, offense go score the ball — we will probably be having a different conversation."

Dallas' season has essentially followed the same pattern as last year, when the offense was good but the defense was not. It has been a "bittersweet" season, as Dallas has showcased the ability to be better than its record at times, but it hasn't resulted in a more consistent performance.

The 2026 Cowboys' offense has been productive more often than not, but their defense has not fared well. Through nine weeks, Dallas is sixth in points per game (27.3) but 25th in points allowed per game (26.2).

Dallas has been in every game it has played this year in the later stages minus an ugly 23-13 loss at the Green Bay Packers only made slightly better by Cowboys wide receiver Ryan Flournoy's last-minute touchdown catch.

The Cowboys have the talent to turn things around, although the schedule is unforgiving. Five of their seven remaining games are against teams with winning records.

Still, Dallas isn't done yet, especially with a superstar aboard like Lamb, who has caught 70 passes for 904 yards and seven touchdowns in nine games this season.

Sunday will be a big day for Dallas. Kickoff is set for 4:25 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes' $325 million KC Current expanded community initiative with six mini-pitches and $900 million soccer movement
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes have helped bring new attention to women's soccer through their ownership of the Kansas City Current.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes have helped bring new attention to women's soccer through their ownership of the Kansas City Current. But their involvement in the club extends beyond the professional game. Through a growing community initiative, the team is helping children discover soccer without the cost of joining traditional programmes. With six mini-pitches across the Kansas City area, the club is building opportunities for young players who might otherwise struggle to access the sport.KC Current expands its mini-pitch initiative across Kansas CityThe latest addition to the Kansas City Current's mini-pitch programme opened at Foreign Language Academy on October 22, 2026. It marked the club's sixth facility and brought another dedicated soccer space to a local school community.The project received funding through a CVS Health grant to the U.S. Soccer Foundation. United Way of Greater Kansas City and the Kansas City Public Schools Education Foundation also supported the effort. KC Current players Avery Clark, Mary Long, Rocky Rodríguez and Katie Scott attended the opening..The new facility serves both students and neighbourhood residents. Children can use the pitch during school hours, while local families have access after classes. This arrangement gives the space a wider purpose than a regular school sports facility.The initiative has developed over several years. Earlier mini-pitches opened at Ashland Square Park, Central Park and Banneker Elementary School. The club also expanded its work to Kansas City Girls Preparatory Academy in 2025.For the Mahomes family, the project adds a community dimension to their involvement with the NWSL club. Their ownership has helped raise the Current's profile, while the mini-pitch programme gives the organisation another way to connect with local families..Patrick and Brittany Mahomes' KC Current focuses on youth access to soccerThe mini-pitch programme forms part of the U.S. Soccer Foundation's Safe Places to Play initiative. Its wider goal is to create safe and accessible spaces where children can enjoy soccer, particularly in communities with fewer sporting facilities.The foundation reports that it has helped establish more than 900 mini-pitches nationwide. It also says 87% of its programming is offered free or at reduced rates, highlighting the role affordable access plays in youth participation.However, the long-term value of Kansas City Current's programme will depend on more than the number of pitches it opens. Regular use, proper maintenance and access for children from different backgrounds will matter just as much.There are also opportunities to measure how many young players benefit, whether girls receive equal access and how often neighbourhood residents use the facilities outside school hours.As the Kansas City Current continues to grow, its community work offers another way to build a lasting connection with the city. articles.title: Dick Hoak Dies at 86, Longtime Steelers Player, Coach Won 5 Super Bowls
articles.summary: Former Pittsburgh Steelers running back Dick Hoak, who won five Super Bowls during his 35-season tenure as the team's offensive backfield and running backs coach and made the team's Hall of Honor, passed away at the age of 86 on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Former Pittsburgh Steelers running back Dick Hoak, who won five Super Bowls during his 35-season tenure as the team's offensive backfield and running backs coach and made the team's Hall of Honor, passed away at the age of 86 on Wednesday.

Steelers President Art Rooney II released a statement.

Hoak, a former Penn State star, played for the Steelers from 1961-1970. He amassed 5,417 yards from scrimmage and 33 touchdowns. Hoak made the 1968 Pro Bowl in his best-ever season, which included 1,111 yards from scrimmage (858 rushing yards, 253 receiving yards) and 4.9 yards per carry.

After one season coaching high school football, Hoak joined the Steelers' coaching staff under head coach Chuck Noll in 1972. He held the offensive backfield coach's position until 1991, when Noll retired.

Hoak was the only coach retained when Bill Cowher took over in 1992, and he assumed a new title, running backs coach. Hoak remained with the Steelers through Cowher's 15 seasons as the Steelers' head coach before they both retired after the 2006 campaign.

Hoak ended up being part of the Super Bowl IX, X, XIII, XIV and XL-winning teams. He coached a host of NFL and Steelers legends, including four in the team's Hall of Honor: Franco Harris, Jerome Bettis, Rocky Bleier and Willie Parker. The Harris-Bleier backfield, of course, was a big reason why the Steelers' dynasty emerged in the 1970s.

The Steelers' backfield enjoyed great success at times even after the 1970s and especially behind Bettis in the 1990s and 2000s.

"As a coach, he's a running back's dream," Bettis said in 2004, per Bob Labriola of Steelers.com. "He gives you the freedom of running to where you feel, but he also gives you an understanding of the play and the philosophy."

Other running backs under Hoak's watch gained 1,000 or more yards from scrimmage in a single season, including Barry Foster (2,034 yards from scrimmage in 1992), Merril Hoge (two 1,000-yard seasons) and Frank Pollard (back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons in 1984 and 1985).

Numerous people expressed their condolences and fond remembrances, including Hoge and ex-Steeler defensive back (and Hall of Fame head coach) Tony Dungy.

Hoak was married 54 years to his wife, Lynn, who passed away in 2019. They are survived by three children and seven grandchildren.

articles.title: Justin Jefferson Reacts to Kirk Cousins' Vikings Return After Raiders Trade Amid Frustration
articles.summary: Justin Jefferson has his former quarterback back in the building.
articles.body:
Justin Jefferson has his former quarterback back in the building.

The Minnesota Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders on Tuesday ahead of the deadline, reuniting him with Jefferson. Following the trade, Jefferson praised Cousins' leadership.

"It's just kind of a joy to hear him take over and be a leader in the meeting room, on the field," Jefferson told reporters Thursday. "It's definitely a cool little situation, for sure."

Cousins played for the Vikings from 2018 to 2023, throwing to Jefferson for four seasons. Jefferson had the best seasons of his career with Cousins throwing to him, including in 2022, when he had 1,809 yards and eight touchdowns.

Cousins likewise had his best seasons in Minnesota when his top target was Jefferson, and they'll look to pick up where they left off.

Cousins signed with the Raiders over the offseason after two years with the Atlanta Falcons, and he's had a strong start to the year despite Las Vegas' struggles. He's thrown for the fifth-most yards (2,340) and the second-most touchdowns (20).

Jefferson, meanwhile, has had a down year amid what has been a slow start to the year offensively for the Vikings.

With Cousins now under center again, the 6-2 Vikings will try to get their offense going to keep up with their outstanding defense. If all of that comes together, Minnesota will have all the makings of a Super Bowl contender.

articles.title: Seahawks’ Drew Lock pinpoints silver lining of nagging oblique injury before Week 10 start
articles.summary: It doesn’t seem Seattle Seahawks quarterback Drew Lock is in serious trouble of missing the reigning Super Bowl champions’ upcoming Week 10 game against the...
articles.body:
It doesn't seem Seattle Seahawks quarterback Drew Lock is in serious trouble of missing the reigning Super Bowl champions' upcoming Week 10 game against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday.

Lock suffered an oblique injury during a Week 9 win over the Arizona Cardinals, raising concerns about his availability for the Raiders game.

In the 17-3 win at Lumen Field in Seattle over the Cardinals, Lock started in place of Sam Darnold and threw for 175 passing yards and a touchdown with zero interceptions, while completing 19 of his 28 passes. He also rushed five times for 16 yards. Darnold sat out that contest with a quad injury, and he will miss another, with Lock expected to continue starting versus the Raiders.

Lock and the Seahawks enter Week 10 with a 5-4 record, good for second in the NFC West standings and behind the San Francisco 49ers' 7-1 slate.
